questions: For the overwriting rule, does 'overwrite' mean that the new color completely replaces the old one, even if the new color is white (i.e., should white overwrite black to become '.' or does white mean 'do not color' and thus leave existing black cells unchanged)?
Are the row and column indices 1-indexed as stated, and does the output string S_i correspond exactly to row i (1-indexed) with characters for columns 1 to N?
What characters should be used for black and white in the output? The example uses '#' for black and '.' for white, but is that mandatory or can any two distinct characters be used?
When i is even and we fill with white, does that mean we set cells to white (e.g., '.'), or does it mean we leave them unchanged (i.e., skip coloring)?
Is N guaranteed to be positive? The constraint says 1 ≤ N ≤ 50, so yes, but what about N=1? Should the single cell be colored based on i=1 (odd) and j=1, so black?
Does the rectangular region from (i,i) to (j,j) include both boundary cells? That is, is it inclusive of all cells with row between i and j and column between i and j?

If i > j, the operation does nothing. But for i where i ≤ j, we fill the square. For even i, if we fill with white, does that overwrite previous colors to white, or does it mean 'do not color' (so previous colors remain)?
Should the output be printed exactly as described, with no extra spaces or newlines beyond the N lines each of length N?
